newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's power industry to be liberalised - minister.
newsitem.headline: Italy's power industry to be liberalised - minister.

text.p: Italy's power generation and distribution industry will be liberalized in parallel with the planned privatisation of state power utility Enel, Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani was quoted as saying.
Bersani said he was also confident that state telecoms group Stet could be sold to private investors before the end of March 1997.
"We have a very clear idea that you cannot pass from a public monopoly to a private one," Bersani told Milan daily Corriere della Sera in an interview.
Enel is one of a number state-owned enterprises, including Stet, which the government has said it wants to privatise without delay.
Bersani said the liberalization of the power sector would be carried out gradually.

"It is clear that the loss of public control will happen in parallel with the liberalization of the sector," said Bersani. "It will be a gradual process, which does not mean either slow or fake," he added.

Regarding Stet, Bersani said the government could still meet its target of privatising it in the first quarter of next year even though legislation setting up a body to regulate the sector has not yet been passed.
"I don't see forces that are really hostile to the privatisation. It's a difficult process, but we will find a solution," he added.
Post and Telecommuniations Minister Antonio Maccanico has said the government could pass legislation instituting a regulatory authority for the industry by decree.
